messages.content: Write the engineering culture section of a careers page. Around 250 words.

output:
## How we build

Teams here are three to five people, and a team owns its service from the design doc through the 3 a.m. page. There is no separate ops group to hand it to. If you built it, your name is on the runbook.

Review is mandatory and it is quick. Median time to a first comment is under two hours, because we treat a stalled pull request as a defect in our process rather than a lapse in manners. Reviewers argue. That is fine. What we don't do is let a disagreement sit for a week waiting on someone senior to break the tie — if two engineers can't settle it in a day, they take the reversible option and move.

We ship on merge. No release train, no Thursday cutoff, no change advisory board. Roughly forty deploys a day go out across the fleet, and a rollback is one command and about ninety seconds. That second number is why we can afford to be wrong in public.

Writing carries weight. Anything longer than two weeks of work starts as a design doc, and the doc gets the same scrutiny the code will.

Our interview has no whiteboard algorithms in it. You spend a day on a real problem from our backlog, with one of us pairing, and we pay you for the day.

On-call is one week in six. Pages that fire twice go on the next sprint board as work, not as folklore passed to whoever is unlucky enough to be holding the pager.

---

Two things worth knowing before this goes live:

- **The numbers are placeholders.** Forty deploys a day, ninety-second rollback, two-hour review median, one-week-in-six on-call, paid interview day — I invented all of them because you didn't give me yours. Swap in the real figures or cut the sentence. A careers page that overstates on-call load is the fastest way to lose someone in month three.
- I wrote it company-agnostic since no company was named. It's a drop-in section, no brand voice imposed.

It clears this repo's own `slopwatch` gate (`lint_text`, no blocking issues), for whatever that's worth as a smoke test.
